outcome: quality of life (measured by Incontinence Quality of Life Questionnaire and Incontinence Severity Index)
cohort: This study included 150 women, 60 years of age or older, receiving treatment for urodynamic stress urine incontinence at various university hospitals.
finding: Obesity reduces older women's quality of life ratings and influences the severity of urodynamic stress incontinence.
mod_finding: There was no discernible difference between the two groups' mean gravidity, parity, or prior delivery modes.
